case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination of parental rights, holding the parent had adequate notice of the court-ordered specific steps and of the consequences of failing to comply with them, and that an adverse inference could be drawn from his refusal to submit to a drug test.
key_cases.relevance: This is the leading Connecticut decision on the notice function of court-ordered specific steps and their evidentiary effect.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the respondent had adequate notice of the consequences of his failing to adhere to the specific steps ordered by the trial court

key_cases.holding: The court held that although an adverse inference may be drawn from a parent's failure to testify at a termination trial, the trial court must give the parent prior notice of its intent to draw such an inference.
key_cases.relevance: It treats the court-ordered service expectations as the measure of the parents' rehabilitative status for the particular child.
key_cases.quote: Consequently, the respondents were entitled to be notified by the court of the prospect that an adverse inference might be drawn from their silence.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a parent who shows the factors that caused her removal as guardian have been satisfactorily resolved is entitled to a presumption that reinstatement of guardianship is in the child's best interests, which the opposing party must rebut by clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: The 'factors that resulted in removal' the parent must resolve are the counseling, therapy and parenting-class conditions imposed by court order.
key_cases.quote: We also conclude that the party opposing reinstatement must rebut this presumption by clear and convincing evidence.

key_cases.holding: The court held that termination of parental rights on the acts-of-commission-or-omission ground in § 17a-112 (j)(3)(C) may not rest on predictive harm, but affirmed the judgments because the amended petitions extended the adjudicatory date so that the parents' postremoval conduct, which actually harmed the child, proved the ground.
key_cases.relevance: The parents' conduct after removal, measured against what the department asked of them, is what supplied the actual harm the statute requires.
key_cases.quote: We agree with the respondents that a termination of parental rights pursuant to § 17a-112 (j) (3) (C) may not be based upon predictive harm.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the commissioner failed to prove by clear and convincing evidence that the department made reasonable efforts to reunify a medically fragile child with his father under § 17a-112 (j)(1), because the department never put the child's current medical information before the trial court, and it reversed the Appellate Court's contrary judgment.
key_cases.relevance: It measures the adequacy of the service plan the department built for an out-of-country parent against the child's actual, changing medical needs.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that the commissioner did not meet the burden of demonstrating that the department did "everything reasonable" under the circumstances to reunite the respondent with Oreoluwa

content_required: The parent or guardian has the right to counsel and must be so informed by the judge
If the parent or guardian is unable to afford counsel, counsel will be provided
The parent or guardian has the rights of confrontation and cross-examination

The court may also appoint counsel for the parent or guardian without a request if it determines the interests of justice so require (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-136(a)); in a proceeding in which the custody of a child is at issue the judge must provide an attorney for the child

Cost of appointed counsel in the civil juvenile session is shared as agreed by the Division of Public Defender Services and the Judicial Department, and the court may order a party found able to pay to reimburse that cost (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-136(b)(1))
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: Not specified in Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 46b-135 or 46b-136

statutory_basis.citation_text: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46b-135(b) (right to counsel and cross-examination); see also § 46b-136 (appointment of attorney; payment) and § 46b-129(c)(1) (advisement at the preliminary hearing)
